correctness.rationale: Unique canonical ellipsoids are invariant under independent block sign flips, so their quadratic forms split. The exact John and Löwner containment constraints are dual scalar ℓp-versus-ℓ2 Hölder optima with equality at dimension weights. Comparing block volumes to factor John/Löwner extrema yields unique scaling and full contact classifications. The κN/∏κdi factors cancel in the ratio, giving the entropy identity. All p endpoints and p=2 equality cases are explicitly checked. The local standalone checker independently evaluated the scalar formulas and 36,000 sampled constraints; sampling is not proof.

originality.rationale: Full mathematical comparison was made to the generic John/Löwner functional conditions of Ivanov–Naszódi (2022), the specific lp-direct-sum Banach–Mazur distance theorem of Grundbacher–Kobos (2026), and earlier John-type ellipsoid characterizations (Klartag 2003). The new theorem supplies exact volume-extremal canonical ellipsoid matrices for arbitrary factors, all contact points, and the strict dimension-entropy ratio. Neither the general criterion alone nor the Banach–Mazur distance formula entails this fully solved volume optimization or equality classification without additional analysis. Query coverage is not proof of novelty; residual classical-prior risk is reported.
residual_risks: Older Banach-space or convex geometry literature may formulate the same block-extremal ellipsoid identity under free sums, product ellipsoids, or tensor norm language. No assertion of exhaustive literature coverage.

value.rationale: The geometrically motivated task is simultaneous canonical-ellipsoid recovery for arbitrary ℓp sums, where the Banach–Mazur distortion answer does not determine either ellipsoid. The result classifies all factor shapes, dimensions, p endpoints, all equality/contact points, and opposite one-block/all-block transitions, with a strict entropic volume distortion law. This is a complete structural and quantitative classification, not a single arbitrary parameter or a recomputed known table.
